page: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a general-purpose virtual machine offering 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of system memory, matching a balanced 1:4 CPU-to-memory ratio. Powered by an Intel Xeon processor running at 2.8 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, it provisions 4 physical cores with two threads per core. The processor includes 33 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512F, AVX-512 VNNI, and AES. The instance contains no bundled local storage, requiring network-attached disk storage, and excludes dedicated GPU accelerators.

Benchmark testing positions the n2-standard-8 squarely within the median range for standard multi-core compute and data-processing tasks. It records a multi-core Geekbench score of 4464.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 8292.45, alongside 50.27 GB/s of large-block uncached memory read bandwidth. Network and cache throughput demonstrate stable enterprise capability, registering 7.12 million operations per second in Redis SET evaluations and 6.9 GB/s in static web serving benchmarks. Conversely, single-threaded processing represents a tradeoff; stress-ng single-core performance, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and image processing register in the bottom quartile of evaluated cloud instances.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and balanced resource density provide consistent multi-threaded compute without incurring overhead for unused accelerator hardware or excessive memory allocations. Because bundled local storage and public IPv4 addresses are omitted, base platform costs stay directly aligned with compute and memory utilization. This hardware profile functions reliably for mid-tier web serving, microservices architectures, continuous integration build nodes, caching tiers, and general-purpose database hosting.
description: Google Cloud Platform n2-standard-8 is a balanced general-purpose virtual machine equipped with 8 vCPUs and 32 GB of RAM across an x86_64 Intel Xeon architecture. Operating at a base frequency of 2.8 GHz, it features 4 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, 33 MB of shared L3 cache, and AVX-512 VNNI vector extensions. The instance provisions no discrete GPU hardware and offers no local disk storage, requiring network-attached storage solutions. In benchmark testing, the n2-standard-8 shows steady median performance in multi-core metrics, achieving a PassMark CPU score of 8292.45, 7.12 million Redis SET operations per second, and 6.9 GB/s in static web serving throughput. Single-core performance and heavy decompression tasks occupy the lower performance quartile. The standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio provides predictable cost efficiency for general enterprise tasks, making it suited for application servers, microservice clusters, CI/CD runners, and mid-sized database workloads.
